avoid_when: Avoid for content-heavy slides requiring bullets, charts, or detailed explanation.
Avoid when the presentation has no author, affiliation, or date metadata.
Avoid for section dividers or closing pages.
families.description: A formal institutional cover slide with a dominant title banner, centered author attribution, and presentation date.
families.name: cover-hero
selection_hints: Use as an academic, research, or institutional presentation cover.
Choose when the opening slide needs a prominent title plus author and date information.
Works best for concise titles and formal conference or laboratory branding.

avoid_when: Avoid for content-heavy slides, detailed summaries, or slides requiring multiple information blocks.
Avoid when a call to action, contact details, or audience questions must be displayed.
families.description: A sparse institutional closing page centered on a prominent thank-you message in a wide horizontal banner.
families.name: closing-hero
selection_hints: Use as the final closing slide of a formal academic, research, or institutional presentation.
Choose when a single short thank-you message should dominate the page.

avoid_when: Avoid when the page needs raw data tables or several independent visualizations.
Avoid when the message is qualitative and does not require a prominent evidence graphic.
Avoid when more than one explanatory text block is needed.
families.description: A split evidence slide pairs concise comparison takeaways on the left with a dominant quantitative chart on the right.
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for a data-backed model, product, or category comparison.
Use when a large chart should be paired with a concise interpretation or takeaway list.
Best for presenting one primary quantitative visualization with supporting commentary.

avoid_when: Avoid when the content does not include a workflow, system architecture, or process visual.
Avoid when several independent data views or a text-only narrative are required.
families.description: A titled split-layout content slide pairs concise workflow highlights on the left with a large detailed process diagram on the right.
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for explaining a workflow with a concise textual overview beside a detailed process diagram.
Use when the audience needs both high-level takeaways and a supporting technical visual.

avoid_when: Avoid when the topic cannot be supported by a single explanatory visual.
Avoid for dense quantitative analysis or multi-panel dashboards.
Avoid when several equally weighted text sections are required.
families.description: A title-led split content slide pairs concise explanatory bullets on the left with a large supporting diagram on the right.
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for explaining the importance, benefits, or rationale of a topic.
Use when concise talking points should be paired with one substantial explanatory visual.
Works well for technical or academic presentations that need a clear text-and-diagram composition.

avoid_when: Avoid when no chart, matrix, or other analytical visual is available.
Avoid when the page needs multiple data views or a detailed methodology discussion.
Avoid for image-led storytelling or side-by-side comparisons.
families.description: A research-style evidence slide featuring a large correlation heatmap with concise interpretive takeaways beneath it.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for presenting one dominant analytical chart followed by concise interpretation.
Choose when a correlation matrix, heatmap, or similar evidence visual is the main focus.
Works well for research findings with two to four short takeaway bullets.

avoid_when: Avoid when the presentation needs a visual roadmap, timeline, or detailed section descriptions.
Avoid when there are more agenda items than can fit as a short, readable list.
families.description: A clean agenda page with a prominent heading and a spacious vertical list of major presentation sections.
families.name: agenda-title_body
selection_hints: Use near the beginning of a presentation to preview a short sequence of major sections.
Choose when a simple, text-led agenda with four or similarly few items is sufficient.

avoid_when: Avoid when the content requires charts, images, tables, or multiple independent visual panels.
Avoid for a cover, section divider, or highly visual storytelling slide.
Avoid when more than a few concise hierarchical points must be presented.
Avoid when the content needs visuals, charts, tables, or data-heavy evidence.
Avoid when more than two major topic groups must be presented.
Avoid when a highly compact or image-led layout is preferred.
families.description: A clean academic content slide with a prominent top heading and a spacious hierarchical bullet list below.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for a conventional informational slide organized under a single clear heading.
Best for explaining a topic through a small number of main points and indented supporting details.
Choose when a clean, text-led academic or technical presentation style is appropriate.
Use for a straightforward explanatory content slide with a prominent heading and hierarchical bullets.
Best for organizing two major concepts with a few supporting details each.
Choose when clarity and ample whitespace are more important than visual storytelling.
